scope: Phase A: public documentation only. No account access, provider contact or remote experiment. Checked for the 2026-11-01 investigation.

facts.subject: Workers Free HTTP CPU and isolate memory
facts.finding: 10 ms CPU per HTTP invocation and 128 MB per isolate including WASM; local workerd is not plan enforcement evidence.

facts.subject: SQLite DO Free CPU entitlement
facts.finding: DO table/default and reset descriptions say 30 seconds; introduction/FAQ also refer to Workers plan/per-invocation limits. No explicit unambiguous Free CPU override was established.

facts.subject: Browser Run Free availability and quota
facts.finding: Available on Free; 600 browser seconds/day shared across methods, three concurrent browser sessions/account, one new instance/20 seconds. Further launches after daily exhaustion return 429 until the next UTC day.

facts.subject: Browser Run Free numeric memory and CPU allocation
facts.finding: No authoritative numeric browser RAM/CPU entitlement was found in the reviewed public pages. Separate Chrome process execution does not prove sufficient resources for this workload.

facts.subject: Browser session shutdown
facts.finding: Default 60-second inactivity timeout is not a 60-second active-task limit. Unclosed sessions continue consuming time; explicit close and failure handling are required.

facts.subject: Local Browser Run feature parity
facts.finding: FAQ reports a local-development request limit of 1 MB. Plain local Playwright is used here; no remote binding is enabled to overcome that limit.

facts.subject: Browser content handling
facts.finding: FAQ describes ephemeral submitted HTML/generated-output processing and no Browser Sessions caching. Optional recordings and crawl have longer retention. Coverage for this custom binary/WASM validation and failure paths still needs clarification.

facts.subject: Actual account and absolute project billing protection
facts.finding: Public Free availability does not verify the owner's account plan, other account usage, activation requirements or a zero-charge configuration. No actual settings were accessed. No paid fallback or R2 is authorized.
